title: Inside My Control
prompt_text: What was inside my control today, and what was outside my control?
top_tip: Separate the two clearly. Then spend most of your writing on what you could choose: your effort, words, attitude, preparation or response.
task_intro:
Reflection is a chance to think carefully about your day.

There is no perfect answer. Choose a real moment, describe what happened, and think about what you can learn from it. Try to focus on your choices, your response, and what you might do next time.

title: The Treasure Map
prompt_text:
You find an old treasure map hidden inside a library book.

top_tip: Make each solution create the next problem.
task_intro:
Fortunately / Unfortunately is a story that keeps changing direction.

Begin with the prompt. Then alternate between good news and bad news:

Fortunately... something helpful happens.
Unfortunately... a new problem appears.
Fortunately... things improve again.

Keep switching until you reach an ending.
category_top_tip: Every new sentence should change the situation. Do not simply say something is good or bad — make something actually happen because of it.

title: Should Homework Be Banned?
prompt_text: Should children have homework after a full day at school?
top_tip: Think about learning, free time, family life and whether all homework is equally useful.
task_intro:
Persuasion means trying to convince somebody.

Choose a clear position, then give your strongest reasons. A powerful argument also thinks about what somebody on the other side might say.

You do not have to choose the answer you think an adult would prefer. You need to make the strongest case you can.
category_top_tip:
Use this simple structure:

My position: say exactly what you think.

My reasons: give two or three strong reasons.

An example: show why one reason matters.

The other side: mention a reasonable objection.

My reply: explain why you still think your position is stronger.
source_reference: user:ADLE Review Writing Challenge — Teaching Content Handoff:2026-08-26
